task_freshAdversarialAttack.methodology: Constructed and directly executed (via scratch tsx probes, then formalized into the new test file) synthetic cases in every category the Part B charter named as an attack vector: nested numbering with inconsistent capitalization, headings immediately following a footnote marker, headings inside a defined-term block, and a multi-column layout collapsed to plain text. Before treating any positive finding as a genuine defect, independently grepped all 4 real fixture packages (fwrg/lsb/conmed/dsgr - both .txt fixtures and the raw CONMED .htm sources) to confirm none of the surfaced shapes occur in real fixture text today (they do not - each finding is a currently-synthetic, forward-looking gap, not a real-fixture regression).
task_freshAdversarialAttack.categoryResult_definedTermBlock: NO DEFECT FOUND. A heading-shaped label used as a quoted defined-term subject (e.g. '"Section 6.01 Indebtedness" shall mean...') is correctly rejected - it never reaches the plausibility gate as a false positive. The gate's signal-based (not phrase-based) design generalizes correctly here.

categoryResult_inconsistentCapitalizatio.description: A lowercase-keyword heading ('section 6.02 Liens.') that is NOT at a literal line start is completely invisible to the parser, even when genuinely, correctly preceded by real sentence-terminal punctuation. Root cause: SECTION_PATTERNS[0] (the shape-based, non-line-anchored primary pattern) and ARTICLE_PATTERNS[0] both require the LITERAL case 'Section'/'SECTION'/'ARTICLE' (no `i` regex flag) - only the line-anchored fallback patterns (SECTION_PATTERNS[1..3], ARTICLE_PATTERNS[1]) carry the `i` flag. A continuous-prose document with no newlines at all - the module's OWN doc-comment names this exact real style as FWRG's own certified fixture convention - can never fall back to a line-anchored pattern, so a lowercase-keyword heading there would be silently dropped regardless of how much positional evidence surrounds it. This is a direct structural recurrence of the ORIGINAL historical defect ARTICLE_PATTERNS' own doc-comment describes (line-anchored-only patterns going blind on a newline-free document), just triggered by keyword CASE instead of by newline absence.
categoryResult_inconsistentCapitalizatio.reproducedAt: tests/certification/part-b-recert-blocker1-independent-adversarial.test.ts, describe block 1 (3 tests: defect + 2 isolating controls)
categoryResult_inconsistentCapitalizatio.realFixtureCheck: grep -oP '\bsection\s+\d+\.\d+' across all DSGR .txt / FWRG .txt / LSB .txt fixtures and a case-insensitive sweep of the raw CONMED .htm sources: 0 hits of a lowercase 'section' keyword anywhere in any real fixture today.

categoryResult_footnoteMarker.description: A footnote-reference-shaped bare 1-2 digit run glued directly (no surrounding whitespace) onto real sentence-terminal punctuation - the shape a superscript footnote marker collapses to under plain-text PDF extraction - defeats BOTH positional signals when only a single newline separates it from the next heading: signal (B) fails because the glued digit, not the period, is now the real last character; signal (A) fails because only one newline (not two) remains. Reproduces identically for SECTION and ARTICLE candidates. When it drops a real ARTICLE, the consequence is not merely a missing index entry but genuine rank-stack corruption: the ARTICLE's real child SECTION is silently re-parented to parentSectionRef=null instead of the correct ARTICLE ref - directly reproducing BLOCKER-1's own named failure class ('rank-stack corruption'), in the opposite direction from the original certified defect (a real parent silently vanishing, rather than a spurious node being wrongly accepted).
categoryResult_footnoteMarker.reproducedAt: tests/certification/part-b-recert-blocker1-independent-adversarial.test.ts, describe block 2 (4 tests: SECTION defect + control, ARTICLE defect-with-misparenting + control)
categoryResult_footnoteMarker.realFixtureCheck: grep -coP '\.\d(?=[A-Z\n])' across all real DSGR/FWRG/LSB .txt fixtures: 0 genuine footnote-marker-shaped hits found in any real fixture today (all incidental '.digit' occurrences inspected are ordinary decimal figures, not footnote markers).

categoryResult_multiColumnCollapse.description: A two-column PDF layout collapsed line-by-line into a single linear text stream (a real, common PDF-text-extraction failure mode) can land a genuine heading mid-interleaving, separated from unrelated preceding (other-column) text by only a single newline and no terminal punctuation - the same three-signal failure as the already-documented Category 6 residual, but via a distinct, newly-named real-world mechanism the Part B charter explicitly asked to be probed, not the table/list/signature-block shape Workstream A already examined and disclosed. The dropped section's real title text is then silently absorbed into the PRECEDING section's own owned span - a real content-misattribution, not merely an index omission.
categoryResult_multiColumnCollapse.reproducedAt: tests/certification/part-b-recert-blocker1-independent-adversarial.test.ts, describe block 3 (1 test, asserting both the missing node and the absorbed content)

categoryResult_pageArtifactAllCaps.description: Discovered while re-attacking RX-GAP-1's own fix from a fresh angle (not one of the charter's four named categories, but the same case-sensitivity root cause recurring a third time). RX's own fix claims to recognize 'an optional "Page " label' (see the stripTrailingPageNumberArtifact doc-comment and 03-blocker1-structural-remediation.json's own test matrix, which tested 'Page N' and lowercase 'page N'), but the actual regex `(?:[Pp]age\s+)?` recognizes 'Page '/'page ' only - never the ALL-CAPS 'PAGE ' running-footer/header convention, which is at least as common a real rendering convention as mixed-case 'Page'. An ALL-CAPS-labeled page number between two single newlines is therefore NOT discounted as a decorative artifact at all; the real double-newline signal it should expose never reaches signal (A), and the following real heading is silently dropped - the exact class of failure RX-GAP-1 itself was built to close, recurring via case rather than via whitespace collapse.
categoryResult_pageArtifactAllCaps.reproducedAt: tests/certification/part-b-recert-blocker1-independent-adversarial.test.ts, describe block 4 (3 tests: defect + 2 isolating controls for the Title-Case and lowercase variants RX's own fix actually tested)

task_freshAdversarialAttack.sharedRootCause: Three of the four genuine findings (inconsistent-capitalization SECTION/ARTICLE, and the ALL-CAPS page-artifact label) are ONE systemic gap appearing at three call sites, not three unrelated defects: every shape-based (non-line-anchored) regex in stage-structure.ts is case-sensitive, while only the line-anchored fallback patterns carry the `i` flag. None of the four findings carry the SAME precision trade-off that justified leaving Workstream A's own Category 6 residual unfixed (loosening case-sensitivity or tolerating a short glued footnote digit before the plausibility checks would not reopen any of the 7 certified STRUCT-1 false-positive sites, all of which fail on citation CONTENT/position grounds unrelated to letter case or footnote digits) - these are therefore reported as genuine, currently-unaddressed gaps, not a reasoned, examined boundary.

blocker1.dispositionRationale: The two specific fixes RX Workstream A claimed (page-number-artifact whitespace preservation; SECTION_PATTERNS unionMatches) both independently reconfirmed sound under fresh probing angles including a harder 3-way mixed-convention case and a dedicated precision re-attack. All 7 originally-certified anomaly sites remain independently reconfirmed at 0, with all 5 distinct DSGR spans independently re-derived byte-identical. However, this Part B pass's own fresh adversarial construction - directly in the categories the charter named as attack vectors - found 4 genuine, general, reproducible false-negative defects in stage-structure.ts (lowercase-keyword mid-sentence heading invisibility for SECTION and ARTICLE alike; a footnote-marker-glued single-newline heading drop for SECTION and ARTICLE alike, with demonstrated real parentage corruption - a direct instance of BLOCKER-1's own named 'rank-stack corruption' failure class - on the ARTICLE case; a multi-column-layout-collapse heading drop with demonstrated content misattribution; and an ALL-CAPS 'PAGE' running-footer label not recognized by RX's own widened artifact regex, discovered while re-attacking that very fix). None occur in the real FWRG/LSB/CONMED/DSGR fixtures today (independently confirmed absent by direct grep across every real fixture file), so none constitute a live-fixture regression, and none carry the same precision-vs-recall trade-off that justified Workstream A's own disclosed, deliberately-unaddressed Category 6 residual. Per this phase's own charter ('If you find a genuine defect, disposition STILL_OPEN or NEW_COUPLED_BLOCKER_DISCOVERED... If everything holds, disposition CERTIFIED_CLOSED'), CERTIFIED_CLOSED is not available. STILL_OPEN (not NEW_COUPLED_BLOCKER_DISCOVERED) is the correct disposition because these are not an architecturally distinct new blocker - they are BLOCKER-1's own named failure class (structural heading / rank-stack corruption), still open against attack vectors this remediation round did not test. Per the production-freeze rule, no production code was modified to fix any of this - all 4 findings are reported as evidence only, pinned in the new test file, for a human or a future remediation pass to act on.
